prompt:
Points $A$ and $B$ have position vectors $\mathbf a=\begin{pmatrix}2\\-1\\3\end{pmatrix}$ and $\mathbf b=\begin{pmatrix}5\\3\\3\end{pmatrix}$.

**(a)** Find $\overrightarrow{AB}$. **[1]**

**(b)** Find $|\overrightarrow{AB}|$ and a unit vector in the direction of $\overrightarrow{AB}$. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $\overrightarrow{AB}=\mathbf b-\mathbf a=\begin{pmatrix}3\\4\\0\end{pmatrix}$ **(A1)**

**(b)** $|\overrightarrow{AB}|=5$ **(A1)**; unit vector $\dfrac15\begin{pmatrix}3\\4\\0\end{pmatrix}$ **(A1)**

**Common mistake:** $\mathbf a-\mathbf b$. “From $A$ to $B$” is end minus start.

prompt: $ABCD$ is a parallelogram with $\overrightarrow{AB}=\mathbf u$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}=\mathbf v$. Express $\overrightarrow{DC}$ and $\overrightarrow{BD}$ in terms of $\mathbf u$ and $\mathbf v$.
markscheme:
$\overrightarrow{DC}=\mathbf u$ — same length and direction as $\overrightarrow{AB}$, so it is the same vector even though it starts elsewhere **(A1)**

$\overrightarrow{BD}=\overrightarrow{BA}+\overrightarrow{AD}=-\mathbf u+\mathbf v$ **(A1)**

prompt:
**(a)** Write $3\mathbf i-2\mathbf k$ as a column vector. **[1]**

**(b)** Find $|3\mathbf i-2\mathbf k|$. **[1]**
The vectors $\begin{pmatrix}2\\p\\6\end{pmatrix}$ and $\begin{pmatrix}3\\-6\\q\end{pmatrix}$ are parallel. Find $p$ and $q$.
markscheme:
Parallel means one is a scalar multiple of the other: $\begin{pmatrix}3\\-6\\q\end{pmatrix}=k\begin{pmatrix}2\\p\\6\end{pmatrix}$ with $k=\tfrac32$ **(M1)**

$-6=\tfrac32p\Rightarrow p=-4$ **(A1)**; $q=\tfrac32(6)=9$ **(A1)**

prompt: $OABC$ is a quadrilateral with $\overrightarrow{OA}=\mathbf a$, $\overrightarrow{OB}=\mathbf b$, $\overrightarrow{OC}=\mathbf c$. $P$, $Q$, $R$, $S$ are the midpoints of $OA$, $AB$, $BC$, $CO$. Prove that $PQRS$ is a parallelogram.
markscheme:
$\mathbf p=\tfrac12\mathbf a$, $\mathbf q=\tfrac12(\mathbf a+\mathbf b)$, $\mathbf r=\tfrac12(\mathbf b+\mathbf c)$, $\mathbf s=\tfrac12\mathbf c$ **(M1)(A1)**

$\overrightarrow{PQ}=\mathbf q-\mathbf p=\tfrac12\mathbf b$ **(A1)**; $\overrightarrow{SR}=\mathbf r-\mathbf s=\tfrac12\mathbf b$ **(A1)**

$\overrightarrow{PQ}=\overrightarrow{SR}$, so one pair of opposite sides is equal and parallel, hence $PQRS$ is a parallelogram **(R1)**

prompt:
**(a)** Write $\mathbf v=\begin{pmatrix}-2\\5\\1\end{pmatrix}$ in terms of $\mathbf i$, $\mathbf j$, $\mathbf k$. **[1]**

**(b)** State the component of $\mathbf v$ in the direction of $\mathbf j$. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $-2\mathbf i+5\mathbf j+\mathbf k$ **(A1)**

**(b)** $5$ **(A1)** — each component is the multiple of the corresponding unit base vector.

prompt: A 2D vector has magnitude 10 and makes an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the positive $x$-axis (measured anticlockwise). Write it in component form.

Let $\mathbf a=\begin{pmatrix}3\\1\end{pmatrix}$ and $\mathbf b=\begin{pmatrix}-1\\2\end{pmatrix}$.

**(a)** Find $\mathbf a+\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf a-\mathbf b$. **[2]**

**(b)** Describe how $\mathbf a+\mathbf b$ is found geometrically. **[1]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $\begin{pmatrix}2\\3\end{pmatrix}$ and $\begin{pmatrix}4\\-1\end{pmatrix}$ **(A1)(A1)**

**(b)** Place the tail of $\mathbf b$ at the head of $\mathbf a$ (triangle law); $\mathbf a+\mathbf b$ runs from the tail of $\mathbf a$ to the head of $\mathbf b$ — the diagonal of the parallelogram on $\mathbf a$ and $\mathbf b$ **(R1)**
